private_note: I can't know my group or even estimate the odds, and this choice lasts a generation with no second chance. So I judge each plan by its worst case for me. Hazel's floor of 41 is the highest available, then Birch's 36, then Alder's 32, then Today's 22, and Cedar's 15 is the lowest. Alder beats Today for the bottom groups, so I'd take it over a failed convention. Cedar is the one plan I would block.
statement: None of us knows where we will land, and none of us can work out the odds. Whatever we pick, we live with for a generation. In that position I can't bet on being in the top fifth. I have to ask what happens to me if I turn out to be at the bottom. Hazel gives the lowest group 41 thousand, more than any other plan, and by design it is the highest floor the economy can sustain. Birch and Alder also raise the floor well above today's 22. Cedar drops it to 15, which leaves the people at the bottom worse off and without health coverage. That risk is too big to accept when any of us could be one of them. I'm ranking Hazel first, Birch second and Alder third, and I'd rather the convention fail than adopt Cedar. I urge each of you to ask which plan you could accept if you woke up in the lowest fifth.
